correctness.rationale: For every m≥1, 1<p<2 and every nonzero pair in complex C², Chebyshev Rodrigues yields a signed positive integral representation for the k-th fractional-cosine coefficient; its normalized absolute value strictly grows with balance parameter, while the mean decreases. The entire Fourier series is absolutely summable, so exact grid aliasing plus incompatible first/second-harmonic signs classifies all equality cases. The beta integral, Gamma reflection, and summable Gamma ratio establish the exact series and sharp m^(-p-1) coefficient. The decoded standalone checker passed 1,005 supplementary finite assertions; finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The new exact all-m complex-coefficient regular-grid maximum, Gamma-series constant, strict zero-on-grid extremizer family, and sharp zeta coefficient are absent from the inspected relevant main results of Dai–Kosov. General Marcinkiewicz sampling and standard Fourier aliasing are acknowledged prior ingredients. Public research-record semantic searches compared aliases and related binomial rigidity, finite Fourier moments, and circular polynomial sampling; no searched claim dominated this exact optimization. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment, not independent or exhaustive novelty certification.

value.rationale: The canonical complex two-dimensional circle subspace is a natural exact test case for Marcinkiewicz-type p-moment discretization. A global worst-case over all complex coefficients and all regular-grid phases, a complete zero-on-grid equality classification for every m, and the explicit sharp zeta constant go beyond routine evaluation of one fixed test function. It gives a precise benchmark for deterministic sampling of fractional-power norms without claiming optimality among arbitrary designs or arbitrary dimensions.
